title: MIDI RX conformance vectors
about: A pure-data contract, not shared code. Each vector is a byte stream and the
ordered list of messages a conformant receiver must deliver from it. Both
flow3r-aeiou and play-aeiou run this table against their OWN parser; neither
imports the other's. That is the boundary rule (values, never messages) and
it is why this is JSON rather than a Python module.
It exists because all four MIDI defects found on 2026-08-27 -- two on each
side, see docs/handshake/midi-comparison.md -- would have been caught by it,
and a sync contract you cannot test is a wish. The running-status and
realtime-interleave vectors are exactly the two that adafruit_midi 1.6.0
fails, so a play-aeiou run of this table is expected to go RED until that
library is patched or pre-filtered. That red is the point: it is the interop
blocker made reproducible instead of described.

conventions.bytes: The RX stream, as integers 0..255, in wire order.
conventions.channel: 0-based (wire nibble). Channel 1 on a keyboard is 0 here.
conventions.expect: Every message the stream completes, in order. A receiver that delivers fewer has LOST messages; one that delivers more has invented them.
conventions.note: Absent fields are not asserted -- a vector constrains what it names.

vectors.name: note_on
vectors.why: The baseline. Nothing else means anything if this fails.

vectors.name: note_off
vectors.why: Release velocity is carried, not discarded -- it was discarded here until 2026-08-27.

vectors.name: note_on_velocity_zero_is_still_a_note_on_at_the_wire
vectors.why: The zero-velocity note-off convention is the CONSUMER's job. A parser that silently rewrites it to note_off makes the two indistinguishable, and a sender that means it cannot say so.

vectors.name: note_below_the_piano_range
vectors.why: Notes run 0-127; NOTE_CODE covered only 21-127, so note 0 raised KeyError out of poll() and crashed the reactor. play-aeiou's ghost note is NoteOn(0, 0), so this was reachable across the cable.

vectors.name: channel_is_the_low_nibble
vectors.why: A receiver that ignores the nibble answers every channel.

vectors.name: two_control_changes_in_one_drain
vectors.why: DEFECT 1 (ours). A single-slot store overwrites the first CC in place -- it is lost, not delayed. Pass poll(on_message) so each message is handled as it completes.

vectors.name: three_note_chord_in_one_drain
vectors.why: DEFECT 1 again, and worse: a NoteStack that sees only the last note drops the gate on its release while two keys are still held.

vectors.name: running_status
vectors.why: DEFECT 2 (adafruit_midi 1.6.0). The status byte is sent once and omitted on the following messages. Not optional: it is what keyboards do under load, and skipping it drops 4 bytes and 2 notes.

vectors.name: realtime_byte_inside_a_message
vectors.why: DEFECT 3 (adafruit_midi 1.6.0), and the one that blocks sync.md: a clock tick may legally arrive BETWEEN the data bytes of another message. It must pass through without disturbing it. adafruit_midi destroys the host message AND loses the clock -- and it fires exactly when a transport is running.

vectors.name: active_sensing_inside_a_message
vectors.why: Same rule, the other common real-time byte. Many keyboards send 0xFE continuously while idle.

vectors.name: pitch_bend_centre
vectors.why: 14-bit, LSB first. Centre is 8192, not 0 -- a receiver that concatenates the bytes the other way round bends the wrong way.

vectors.name: pitch_bend_full_up
vectors.why: Both bytes at maximum is 16383, one below a clean power of two.

vectors.name: transport_start_then_clock_then_stop
vectors.why: The sync contract's own alphabet. These are single-byte messages with no data and no channel.

vectors.name: channel_aftertouch
vectors.why: One data byte, not two -- a parser expecting two swallows the next status byte.

vectors.name: a_truncated_message_completes_nothing
vectors.why: A cable pulled mid-message must not deliver a half-parsed note. Silence is the correct output.

vectors.name: a_new_status_abandons_the_unfinished_one
vectors.why: A status byte arriving where a data byte was expected means the previous message will never complete. Resync on it rather than folding it in as data.
